messages:
Carlos (oncall): getting paging alerts for embeddings.prod-us-west — 5xxs + p95 latency spike. Customer ticket from DataForge just came in, they say bulk embedding calls are failing intermittently.

IncBot: ALERT: embeddings.service.prod-us-west 5xx_rate=6.7% over 8m. Trigger: error_rate > 5%. See: https://ops.redwood/alerts/embeddings-177555

Jin: I'm on it. Quick glance at the batcher logs shows repeated GPU runtime failures with `DIMENSION_MISMATCH` coming from embed-xlarge model. Looks like some inputs are 2048 while the model is 1024.

Priya: Whoa — why are clients sending 2048? Our catalog only lists 1024 for embed-xlarge. Could be a new SDK release or an upstream encoder change.

Liam: Repro: ran a synthetic mix of dims (1024 + 2048) hitting the same batch window. GPU kernel fails the whole batch when mixed. Logs below:
```
[batcher] batch_id=9876: assembling tensors -> shapes: [1024,2048,1024]
[runtime] kernel_launch failed: INVALID_ARGUMENT: embedding tensor shape mismatch
stack: runtime/kvcache.cu:145
```

Carlos (oncall): Is this why customers see 5xxs? If so, we need a short-term mitigation before postmortem.

Jin: Yes. Current batcher groups by time only; it doesn't validate per-item dims before concatenating. Small change: validate item.dim == model.dim at enqueue time and return 400 for mismatches. That will prevent kernel failures. I can push a hotfix to the batcher within 15-20 minutes.

Priya: Also, suggestion: add a routing header `X-embedding-dim` so we can partition pools or route to fallback models automatically. Longer term.

Support Team: DataForge repro steps in ticket 10011: curl -X POST https://api.redwood/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"model":"embed-xlarge","inputs":[[0.01,0.02,...(2048 floats)...]]}' — they said intermittent because some microservices started emitting 2048 vectors after a model upgrade.

Liam: Immediate mitigation I can roll: 1) add per-request validation at the ingress (edge proxy) to reject mismatched dims with 400 + helpful message; 2) enable `batch_group_by_dim=true` config on prod-us-west pool to avoid cross-dim mixing. Both are low-risk config changes.

Carlos (oncall): Do the two. Prioritize ingress validation first. If possible, temporarily reduce batch_window_ms to 15ms to lower mixing probability but watch p95.

IncBot: NOTE: config change requested by Liam: batch_group_by_dim=true for pool prod-us-west. Pending deploy.

Jin: Pushed ingress validation patch (edge) — returns 400: "embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1024, received 2048". Patch id: a1b2. Deployed in canary then prod in ~7m.

Liam: Enabled batch_group_by_dim and set batch_window_ms=15 for the embeddings pool. Deploy applied. Monitoring starting...

Carlos (oncall): Monitoring shows errors dropping. 5xx down from 6.7% -> 1.2% in 9 minutes. p95 latency slight increase (~10ms) but acceptable.

IncBot: DEPLOYMENT: embeddings-batcher cfg update by Liam succeeded.

Support Team: Notified DataForge with details and suggested they pin to old encoder or migrate their inference pipeline to emit 1024 vectors. They acknowledged and will roll back the encoder change in staging first.

Jin: For the record, root cause: a partner microservice rolled out a new local encoder (2048-dim) without updating client/model mapping. Because the batcher mixed dims across the same GPU batch window, kernel failed and whole batches returned 5xx. Contributing factors: no ingress validation, batcher grouping by time only.

Priya: Action items (short/mid/long):\n- Short: ingress validation + batch_group_by_dim (done).\n- Mid: add explicit per-dim pools and update routing to use X-embedding-dim header.\n- Long: add automated detection alert: "mixed_dim_batch_failures > 0.1%" + onboarding doc for partners about supported dims and SDK checks.

Liam: Filed ENG-EMB-2027 with details and PR links. I'll take the pool segregation task next sprint.

Carlos (oncall): Keep an eye on the customer ticket. If DataForge still sees failures after their rollback, escalate. I'll keep this incident open for another hour of stable metrics.

Support Team: DataForge replied: "Thanks, the 400s made debugging obvious. We'll revert our encoder in staging and re-run tests. Appreciate the quick fix." :thumbsup:

IncBot: INCIDENT UPDATE: embeddings.service.prod-us-west error spike mitigated. Current 5xx_rate=0.6%. Incident duration so far ~42m. Log: https://redwood.incidents/1775554321

Carlos (oncall): Closing the on-call thread when metrics stable for 1h and support confirms customer regression fixed. Will write postmortem with timeline, logs, and recommended config changes.
